newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-COX CENTURY STRETCHES TASMANIA'S LEAD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-COX CENTURY STRETCHES TASMANIA'S LEAD.

text.p: Tasmania's opening batsman Jamie Cox hit a quicksilver century on Sunday to put his side in a position to press for victory in their Sheffield Shield cricket match against Victoria.
Cox was 102 not out at the close of play on the third day of the four-day match as Tasmania reached 161 without loss in their second innings for a lead of 211 runs.
Victoria had earlier declared their first innings closed on 431 for nine after a century by former Australia test batsman Dean Jones.
Resuming on 220 for three overnight, Victoria finished 50 runs behind Tasmania's first innings of 481 for eight declared.
Cox and opening partner Dene Hills quickly took the initiative for Tasmania, with Hills on 54 not out at the close.

Cox produced his 11th first-class century and the fifth of the match with a cover drive to the boundary as Tasmania sought quick runs ahead of an expected declaration early on Monday. His hundred came from 132 deliveries and included 14 boundaries.
Jones resumed on 130 and went on to make 145 before he was bowled by all-rounder Shaun Young.
Acting as captain in the absence of Australia test leg-spinner Shane Warne, Jones declared his side's innings closed with tail-ender David Saker on 66 not out.
